page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor rated up to 4.2 GHz. Its x86_64 CPU architecture includes modern instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware crypto acceleration. Memory is configured at 32.0 GB RAM, delivering a 1:8 ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 236 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD, and the configuration operates without a dedicated hardware GPU accelerator.

Benchmark evaluations reveal balanced single-threaded execution alongside constrained multi-threaded capacity due to the 2-core / 4-thread count. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 1948.38 and Geekbench single-core scored 1643.0, both falling within average ranges. In contrast, multi-core stress-ng (3991.37) and Geekbench multi-core (3707.0) rank in the lower quartile across cloud servers. Single-threaded gzip compression reached a strong 31.35 GB/sec, while compilation and image processing tasks remain limited by raw core count.

Memory and cache performance show a PassMark memory score of 2264.9, with uncached read throughput measuring 36.24 GB/sec and write throughput at 25.93 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 5.66 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 7.57 GB/sec static web serving throughput. For lightweight machine learning workloads, prompt processing for small 135M parameter models executed at 436.99 tokens/sec.

Because of its 8.0 GB per core resource density and bundled local NVMe SSD scratch capacity, the E4ds_v6 is efficient for workloads requiring substantial RAM footprint without excessive parallel compute needs. Ideal workloads include relational and in-memory caching databases, enterprise middleware, lightweight LLM inference on small models, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines.
